clue.text: Take off from lower ground?

parts.note: sub- is a prefix meaning under or lower, as in subway
a tract is a stretch of land or ground

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the high land and takes off from a lower field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' reads as departing or launching from a place, but it is the arithmetic sense of removing a number.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct a number from another is to take it off the total.

clue.text: Instruct as a group in the main

explanation.surface: Teach a class out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, where fish swim in groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To train or educate someone; also a shoal of fish or whales swimming together in the ocean.

clue.text: The desperado is a party to it

parts.note: a band is a group or party of people

explanation.surface: A gunslinger is involved in the affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a party to' sounds like being involved, but it splits as BAND (a party) + IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw or robber, as a lawless gunman might be called.

clue.text: One's need to be in an organisation that's on the up and up

indicators.note: need to be in means the first piece is placed inside the organisation word

parts.note: a ring is an organised group, such as a spy or drugs ring
one is I, and the apostrophe-s stands for is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: A newcomer must join a thriving firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I + S, which 'need to be in' places inside RING; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Going up steadily, improving or ascending, as prices or a career may be.

clue.text: Like a little company and many a story

parts.note: Co is the short form of company
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number
a parable is a short moral tale

explanation.surface: A small theatre troupe resembles many a tale they perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' is the adjective meaning similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar to, able to be set beside another for measuring.

clue.text: Abandon an over-dry area

explanation.surface: Leave behind a parched stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who deserts abandons his post; an arid region with very little rain is the other sense.

clue.text: Self-centred people get so — it's quite dreadful

indicators.note: dreadful means awful, telling us to mangle the letters of the words before it

parts.note: the letters of it's are taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Vain types become so awful it's unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite dreadful' rearranges GET, SO and ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: People absorbed in themselves and full of self-importance.

clue.text: Heavenly present for use inside and elsewhere

indicators.note: for use inside means the word for present goes within the other piece

parts.note: et al. is Latin et alibi, and elsewhere
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A divine gift meant for indoors and outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means here. Et al. can stand for et alibi, 'and elsewhere', as well as 'and others'.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial or unearthly, too delicate for this world.

clue.text: Note the revolutionary may well appear restrained

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Observe that the rebel may look subdued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as observe, but it is the sol-fa note TE; 'may well appear' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up with a rope or chain to a post, so held back.

clue.text: Beautiful homes — and otherwise!

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, telling us to rearrange the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: An estate agent praises lovely houses, and their opposites too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' turns the letters of HOMES and AND into a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-looking or fine to look at; a striking house can be called beautiful in this way.

clue.text: Wear for formal occasions, which includes work

indicators.note: includes means the word for which holds another piece within it

parts.note: that can stand for which in a relative clause
op, short for opus, is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A dress code note: formal outfits that involve some effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts OP inside THAT, splitting it as T + OP + HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall silk headgear worn with morning dress at weddings and races.

clue.text: Japanese maybe getting into real chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, telling us to jumble the letters of the words beside it

explanation.surface: A Japanese person is caught up in genuine disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' scrambles the letters of INTO and REAL; 'getting' is a link. 'maybe' marks Japanese as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from East Asia was traditionally described with this word; a Japanese person is one example.

clue.text: "No beast so — but knows some touch of pity" (Shakespeare)

definitions.text: "No beast so — but knows some touch of pity" (Shakespeare)

parts.words: "No beast so — but knows some touch of pity" (Shakespeare)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Richard III, where Lady Anne says even the most savage animal feels some pity

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare with one word left out for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is spoken by Lady Anne in Richard III; the missing adjective describes a wild, savage beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means savage or ferocious, the quality of a wild animal.

clue.text: Where one first saw the light!

definitions.text: Where one first saw the light!

parts.words: Where one first saw the light!
parts.note: seeing the light suggests a sudden insight or conversion, but here it means opening one's eyes as a newborn

explanation.surface: Recalling the spot where someone had a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw the light' sounds like a conversion, but it is the first daylight a baby sees.
explanation.definitionFit: The town or house where a person was born.

clue.text: A person coping with a trying job

definitions.text: A person coping with a trying job

parts.words: A person coping with a trying job
parts.note: a trying job reads as a hard one, but it means a job of trying cases in court

explanation.surface: Sympathy for someone stuck in a stressful post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' looks like 'exhausting', but it means hearing cases: the person's work is to try people in a lower court.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay justice or JP whose role is to hear and judge minor criminal cases.

clue.text: Nourishment for those on a strict diet?

definitions.text: Nourishment for those on a strict diet?

parts.words: Nourishment for those on a strict diet?
parts.note: people fasting eat nothing, so their food is a fast, read as a playful paradox

explanation.surface: A question about what dieters should eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means burgers and chips; read literally it is food for people who fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickly prepared takeaway meals such as burgers; read literally, food for those fasting.

clue.text: Enters without asking permission, so is turned out

definitions.text: Enters without asking permission, so is turned out

parts.words: Enters without asking permission, so is turned out
parts.note: describes a person who barges in uninvited and is therefore thrown out

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher who comes in unasked gets thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Barges in where one is not wanted or invited.

clue.text: Fine monarch's judgment

parts.note: fine means thin, as of a fine thread
a king is a monarch; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A good king's ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' reads as excellent, but it means slender.
explanation.definitionFit: One's opinion or reasoning on a matter, as in 'to my way of thinking'.

clue.text: Rub out a thin line, a mistake having been made

indicators.note: a mistake in drawing means the letters before it have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An artist erases a fine stroke after slipping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mistake having been made' rearranges A, THIN, LINE and A into the answer. 'Rub out' reads as erase but is slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub someone out is slang for killing them, and to destroy utterly is the same idea.

clue.text: Took food outside to finish when repelled

indicators.note: outside means the eating word goes around the other piece

parts.note: fed means ate, took food
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone ate outdoors to finish a meal when driven away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps FED around END; 'to' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Warded off or drove back an attacker, as in fended off.

clue.text: Though mean, gain very little

parts.note: mid means middle, the mean point
to get is to gain

explanation.surface: A miser who earns very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' reads as stingy, but it is the average or middle point.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective for something tiny or miniature.

clue.text: Things to be seen to requiring time and trouble

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters of the word before are disturbed

explanation.surface: Jobs needing attention take time and effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns AND into NDA, after AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with at a meeting, from Latin for things to be done.

clue.text: A ruthless man in the City ran things his way

definitions.text: A ruthless man in the City ran things his way

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: A hard-nosed financier controlled the Square Mile as he pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is inside 'CiTY RAN Things'; the whole clue also describes a despot who rules as he likes.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a cruel ruler who governs with absolute power as he pleases.

clue.text: Make notes about cunning back moving quickly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the singing word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes

indicators.note: back means the word for cunning is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: deep can mean shrewd or cunning, as in a deep one

explanation.surface: A crafty student takes notes about devious tactics, then moves off fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEEP into PEED, and 'about' wraps SING around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving faster than the limit, or travelling at a rapid pace.

clue.text: Lay down frock

explanation.surface: Instructions to put a dress on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To decree is to lay down a rule; to frock a cleric is to admit him to holy orders.

clue.text: Casual wear for town

explanation.surface: Relaxed clothing suitable for a trip into town.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted button-up woollen jacket; also Aberteifi, a market town in west Wales.

clue.text: Drop in animal treatment by the vet?

indicators.note: in means one piece is set inside another

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit
to sag is to droop or drop down

explanation.surface: A small amount of medicine for a sick animal, given by the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SAG inside DOE. 'Drop' looks like a droplet of medicine, but it means sag.
explanation.definitionFit: The measured amount of a medicine given is part of veterinary treatment, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Family conflict to some end

parts.note: a feud between clans pursued until some final result, often bloodshed

explanation.surface: A family quarrel carried on until it is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some end' suggests a purpose, but the feud is carried on to a bitter end.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood feud between families, traditionally Corsican or Sicilian, pursued with revenge killings.
